title: Stadium Evacuation Map
statement: A stadium floor plan is a 1,000 × 1,000 grid with walls and 40 exits. Safety staff need, for every seat cell, the walking distance to the nearest exit.
examples: Two exits on a small plan → each cell's distance to the closer exit

approaches.name: One BFS starting from all exits at once
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each cell is visited once; the first visit comes from its nearest exit.

approaches.name: A BFS from each exit, keeping the minimum per cell
approaches.label: valid

approaches.name: A BFS from each seat until it reaches an exit
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: A million searches is far too slow.

approaches.name: Use straight-line distance to the nearest exit
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Ignores walls, so it can be badly wrong.

title: Office Network Merge
statement: An IT team plugs in 200,000 cables one at a time between 100,000 devices and, after each cable, must say whether the whole office is now one network.
examples: 3 devices, cables 1–2 then 2–3 → no, then yes

approaches.name: Union-find with a running count of groups
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each cable is a near-constant merge; one network when the count reaches 1.

approaches.name: Run BFS over all devices after each cable
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: BFS once after all cables
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Fast, but answers only at the end, not after each cable.

approaches.name: Keep a devices × devices reachability matrix
approaches.label: unsuitable

title: Sliding Puzzle Solver
statement: A phone game shows a 2 × 3 sliding puzzle with tiles 1–5 and one gap. The game needs the fewest moves from any shuffled position to the solved one, or to say it is impossible.

approaches.name: BFS over board positions, each written as a string
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Few states; BFS gives the fewest moves and finds impossible positions.

approaches.name: DFS over moves until solved
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Does not give the fewest moves and can loop.

approaches.name: Always move the tile that is farthest from its place
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Gets stuck and is not optimal.

approaches.name: A* search with a distance heuristic
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and faster on big puzzles, but more code than needed for 720 states.
